items.title: TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON and FuzzMarshalRaw are red on Go 1.27: encoding/json escapes U+2028/2029 with SetEscapeHTML(false) now
items.body:
On go1.27.3 (linux/amd64, a WSL2 dev box), on current main:

    go test -tags nogui -run 'TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON|FuzzMarshalRaw' ./internal/gateway/

is red:

    escape false:
         marshalRaw   "[\"line\u2028sep\u2029\"]"
         encoding/json "[\"line\\u2028sep\\u2029\"]"

encoding/json's Encoder changed in Go 1.27: with SetEscapeHTML(false) it now
escapes U+2028 and U+2029 (it left them raw through 1.26, which is what
fastjson's marshalRaw matches and documents at internal/gateway/fastjson.go:1321
"U+2028, U+2029 escaped when escapeHTML, as json.Marshal writes them"). A
one-liner shows it on 1.27.3:

    enc := json.NewEncoder(&b); enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
    enc.Encode([]any{"line\u2028sep\u2029", nil})
    // "[\"line\\u2028sep\\u2029\",null]"  — escaped

CI stays green (it runs 1.26.x), so this only bites local runs on Go 1.27.
FuzzMarshalRaw fails the same way on seed #7.

The call is magpie's: keep fastjson's (json/v2-aligned) raw behavior and pin
the divergence in the test per Go version, or escape with 1.27 when not
escaping HTML to keep the equivalence.

items.title: bug(routing): Codex compaction can reclassify an unchanged native turn when transcript identity changes
items.body:
## Problem

An ongoing Codex task can be classified again after context compaction even though its native turn ID has not changed and no new task was submitted. This adds a classifier call and can make the route depend on the summary instead of the original task.

Observed on v0.1.1330. In one correlated routing/session trace, the parsed route turn changed from 7 to 1 immediately after compaction; a fresh classification appeared for the same native turn. The chosen model happened to stay the same, so this is evidence of duplicate classification, not proof of a model switch or measured monetary loss. No complete production HTTP payload was retained.

## Relevant implementation

At v0.1.1330 (`e00fbdbbc74f9829027a78769cbeb265d6271fb4`), `internal/gateway/rules.go` keys the turn decision by group, conversation identity and `firstWords(req)`, and determines continuation through `turnIn(req)`. Compaction can replace the first user text and renumber the parsed transcript. The v0.1.1363 source inspected also retains this key structure; that release has not been runtime-tested for this report.

## Minimal synthetic reproduction

Use local classifier/provider stubs and the Responses gateway with a Codex client user-agent:

1. Submit a user task with `client_metadata.thread_id="session-a"` and `turn_id="turn-a"` (or the corresponding supported transport metadata). Expect one classifier call.
2. Submit a replacement compacted transcript with different first user text, keeping the same session and native turn. No new task was issued. The current behavior classifies again; expected behavior is to preserve the active turn's decision.
3. Change the native turn to `turn-b`. This must classify again.
4. Also test a genuine native cross-thread delegation arriving inside the same active native turn: it must still establish a new task, rather than being suppressed by session/turn stickiness.

Steps 1–3 were reproduced through the actual gateway handler with loopback stubs. A negative control removing the proposed native-identity hookup makes the compaction assertion fail; restoring it passes. These are protocol-shaped tests, not byte-for-byte production replay.

## Proposed minimal repair (local prototype, not deployed)

- Where supported native metadata exists, bind classification continuity to group + session + native turn (and installation identity when available), rather than mutable transcript first words/parsed turn count.
- Preserve reclassification for a genuine new delegation within an active native turn. Our middleware already exposes the delegation text for classification; a boundary identity distinguishes a new dispatch from its tool continuations.
- Keep legacy behavior for clients without sufficient native identity; exclude prediction/title/description helpers from this binding.
- Preserve existing expiry, rule applicability and capacity checks. Do not pin a model for an entire session or change effort/provider selection.
- Store bounded identity digests, not raw task text, in the continuity state.

This is a repair proposal, not a claim that the prototype is production-ready. Middleware alone cannot reliably control the native classifier cache. Any upstream implementation should also preserve legitimate steering/new-task boundaries and existing concurrency behavior.

## Validation and limits

Local prototype based on v0.1.1330:

- Targeted native-turn, routing, Jev and middleware tests pass with `-race`; `go vet` and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Tests cover compaction continuation, a new native turn, new delegation within a turn, separate sessions, legacy fallback, and removing temporary middleware routing items before provider forwarding.
- Plain full gateway suite completed on both pristine base and patched source: 401.368s and 404.226s. Both fail the same tests: `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (19/30 images with 10 kept), `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, and `FuzzMarshalRaw/seed#7` (U+2028/U+2029 escaping). This is not a full-suite PASS. The image test also has a prior report in #2606.
- Full-package race runs were time-limited and did not complete; targeted race success is not full-package race coverage.
- All validation backends were local stand-ins. No real classifier/model requests or review reruns were made for these tests; no production binary/configuration was replaced.

This report intentionally omits account information, real task text, session IDs, local paths and private logs. Would you prefer a standalone regression test or a minimal patch for review?

items.title: [bug] sessions: a Claude Code fork subagent's copy of its parent's reply is counted twice (branch ready; PRs are collaborators-only)
items.body:
Branch: [fish2lab/magpie `sessions-claude-fork-copy`](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/tree/sessions-claude-fork-copy), one commit, [df11f97](https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie/commit/df11f97d0e16279d889b0f0da8a353b6d903661d), on origin/main 7d075df. I'm filing it as an issue because PRs here are limited to collaborators.

```
git fetch https://github.com/fish2lab/magpie sessions-claude-fork-copy && git cherry-pick df11f97
```

## What's wrong

A Claude Code fork subagent's transcript (`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, here from Claude Code 2.1.302) opens with a `fork-context-ref` line. Next comes a copy of the parent's reply that started the fork, with the same `message.id` and `requestId`, now marked `isSidechain: true` with the fork's `agentId`. Then comes the fork's own prompt. The parent's main file already counts that reply, and the sessions reader dedupes calls only within a file. So `magpie sessions` and the stats count the reply once more for every fork.

## The fix

Subsystem: sessions (`internal/sessions`, the Claude Code reader). No subsystem reference documents how Claude transcripts are counted, so no page changes.

- Trigger: a `fork-context-ref` line. The reader sets `state.ForkHead` and skips assistant lines until the file's first user line. It does this both in the fast path (`claudeLine`) and in the full parse (`claudeFull`). The first user line clears the flag, and everything after it is counted as before.
- Before: the copied reply counted once in the parent's file and again in each fork's file. After: it counts once, in the parent's file.
- State: `ForkHead` is kept in the parse cache (`fork_head`), so a read that resumes inside the head still skips. `cacheVersion` goes from 22 to 23, so files parsed before are read again.
- Files without a `fork-context-ref` line read as before. These include ordinary subagents, workflow agents and main transcripts.

## Verification

Run at df11f97 (on origin/main 7d075df), go1.27.3 darwin/arm64:

- `gofmt -l` is clean.
- Vet is clean: `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.
- Builds are ok: `go build`, `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` and `GOOS=windows go build`.
- `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` in a sandbox HOME with Go's caches pinned: 69 packages ok, including `internal/sessions` (ok, 73s). A few packages are red, and they are red in the same way on origin/main 7d075df without this change:
  - `internal/provider`: #3632 (ok in 71s with `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` skipped)
  - `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON` and `FuzzMarshalRaw` (#3547), `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (#3549), `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (#3680)
  - `internal/plugin`: `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207)
- Broken by hand: I put the old `claude.go` and `sessions.go` back and kept the new test. `TestClaudeForkSubagentCountsParentReplyOnce` then fails with `session: {Input:250 Output:25 CacheRead:30 ...}, want {Input:150 Output:15 CacheRead:20 ...}`. With the change restored, it passes.

I also checked against real data. I copied one real session (its main file and its one fork) into a sandbox, with HOME, the XDG dirs and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` all pointing there, and ran `magpie sessions --json` with binaries built from origin/main and from this branch:

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| input | 238 | 236 |
| output | 153,562 | 150,944 |
| cache read | 24,171,440 | 24,041,229 |
| cache write | 388,781 | 387,933 |

The branch's numbers equal that session's calls deduped by `message.id` + `requestId` across all of its files, as counted by an independent reader, [git-tab](https://github.com/fish2lab/git-tab)'s Claude Code adapter.

Not tried:

- Cowork transcripts, which use the same reader.
- Running on Linux or Windows; only the GOOS vet and builds above were run. The change has no platform code.

## Found while checking, not changed here

I compared 115 sessions from the last 30 days against git-tab, and 100 matched to the cent. Three other differences come from magpie behavior I left alone. I can open a separate issue for any of them if useful:

- `sessions` and the stats price each model's total at its base tier (`p.At(0)` in `sessions.go` and `stats.go`). So Claude Haiku 5.5's rate for prompts above 100K tokens ($0.50/$2.50 per MTok, against $0.10/$0.50) is never applied. One pi session on Haiku 5.5 had identical tokens on both sides. It cost $0.12 in magpie, against $0.52 when each request is priced at its tier.
- DeepSeek's peak-hour price is not applied. It is 2× on weekdays 9:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 Beijing time ([pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing)). Two pi sessions on deepseek-flash that ran entirely in peak hours came out at half their price.
- A forked or resumed Claude Code session copies its parent's history into a new main file under a new `sessionId`. Per-session totals then count the copied calls in both sessions. In one fork the copies made up 95% of its listed cost: $6.62 listed, against $0.31 for its own calls.
